questions.question:
**Direction: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order, except the first part. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.**

It is…

A. who are continually trying to improve

B. not the least talented

C. their dialogue skills,

D. the most talented people
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"DACB."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is about talented people and their dialogue skills.
 
• The first part of the sentence is missing, so we need to start with the part that makes sense: **"It is." **So, the first part is** D.**
 
• The next logical part is** "not the least talented",** which sets up a comparison. So, the next part is A.
 
• The third part should be the one that contrasts with "not the least talented", which is "the most talented people". So, **C must follow A**.
 
• Finally, we need to add the part that explains what the most talented people are doing, which is "who are continually trying to improve their dialogue skills". So, the last part is **B**.
 
• The correct answer is option 1.
 
• **Correct sentence**: 

*It is **the most talented people who are continually trying to improve their dialogue skills, not the least talented**__.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can replace the underlined part of the following sentence.**

It has been raining **__from__** morning.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"since."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"since"** is used to indicate the starting point of a period of time.
 
• It refers to a time (an action that begun in the past and is still continuing).
 
• In this sentence, **"since" **is the most appropriate option as it indicates that the rain started in the morning and is still continuing.
 
 
• **Example**: *We have been married **since**__ 1996.*
 
 
 
• The word **"from"** is used to refer to a place or time at which any event/action/journey starts/initiates. The word since is used to refer to the time passed between then and now.
 __
 
• **Example**: *The movie will run **from**__ 10:00 a.m to 12:00 p.m.*
 
 
 
• The word **"for"** would indicate a duration of time, but it doesn't fit the context of the sentence as it doesn't convey that the rain is still ongoing.
 __
 
• **Example**: *I was waiting **for**__ an hour.*
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

 

**Correct sentence**: *It has been raining __**since**__ morning.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: "For"** indicates a duration of time.

 
 
• **Example**: *"I have been waiting **for**__ two hours."*
 
 
 
• **Option 2: "Though" **indicates a contrast or concession.
 __
 
• **Example**: *"**Though**__ it was raining, we still went for a walk."*
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "Till"** indicates an end point.
 __
 
• **Example**: *"The store is open **till**__ 10 PM."*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

Let the book be read by me.

options.text: Let me had read the book.
Let me have read the book.
Let me please read the book.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Let me read the book."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The rules for changing an imperative sentence from passive to active voice is as follows:

 
 
• In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The subject of the active sentence becomes the agent (or doer) of the action in the passive sentence.
 
• To form the passive voice, use the auxiliary verb "be" + past participle of the main verb.
 
• In this sentence, "let" is already in the passive form, so we only need to change the subject and object.
 
• An imperative sentence in the passive voice has the following form:
 
• Structure:
 
 
• Let + subject + V1 + object. (Active voice)
 
• Let + object + be + past participle of the verb. (Passive voice)
 
• Example: ​
 
 
• *Let us call Riya. (Active Voice)*
 
• *Let Riya be called by us. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Correct sentence: *Let me read the book.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.**

The number of seats **__in the movie theater were reduced__** to comply with the new social distancing guidelines.

options.text: in the movie theater was reduced
in the movie theater were being reduced
of the movie theater were reduced
in the movie theater are reduced

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"in the movie theater was reduced."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part **"theater were reduced."**
 
• According to the subject-verb agreement, a singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject takes a plural verb.
 
• The subject **"number of seats"** is singular, so the verb should also be singular** ("was" instead of "were")**.
 
• **"Of the movie theater" **is grammatically incorrect because** "number of seats"** is not a possession of the theater.
 
• **"Were being reduced"** implies a continuous action, which is not necessary in this context.
 
• **"Are reduced" **is present tense, which is incorrect because the action has already happened in the past.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

**Correct sentence**: *The number of seats **in the movie theater was reduced**__ to comply with the new social distancing guidelines. *

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.**

The tickets had already been booked by my friend.

options.text: My friend already booked the tickets.
The tickets had already booked my friend
My friend had already booked the tickets.
My friend has already booked the tickets.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"My friend had already booked the tickets."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Past Perfect Tense and Active Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a Past Perfect Tense from Active voice to Passive voice:
 
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence, and the verb is changed to its past participle form.
 
 
 
• Structure__: 
 __
 
• Subject + had + V3 + Object (Active Voice)__
 
• Object + had + been + V3 + by + Subject __(Passive Voice)__
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *Disha had arranged the things. *(Active Voice)
 
• *The things had been arranged by Disha.** *(Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• The sentence is in passive voice, with the subject 'tickets' performing the action 'booking'.
 
• To convert it into active voice, we need to make the object 'my friend' the subject and use the past participle form of the verb 'book'.
 
• In this case, we use the past perfect tense 'had already been offered' to show that the action was completed before another past event.
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

 

Correct sentence: *My friend had already booked the tickets.*

• Using the word "reign" in this context emphasizes the direct connection between the ruler featured on the coin and the historical and cultural significance of that period.
